topics.topic: Exact attributes and lifetime semantics contained in OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES
questions: What exact cookie attributes does this constant contain, including Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Domain, expiry and persistence semantics?
Which exact Set-Cookie attributes and values does OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES contain, including Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Domain and any lifetime attribute?

What exact cookie attributes does this newly named constant contain, including Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Domain, persistence or expiry, and are the same attributes required when replacing or clearing the cookie?

quotes:
The session cookie is
  named `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` (`__Host-registry_session`) and set
  with the attributes `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES` holds and no other:
  `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `Path=/` and no `Domain`, which the `__Host-` prefix
  makes a browser require (A13 rule 1), and `SameSite=Strict`, so a browser
  never sends it with a request another site started (owner, 2026-11-24;
  OWASP).

Registry never expires or deletes the cookie: an ended session's
cookie is refused at the session check and replaced by the next sign-in, so
no answer, however late it arrives, can remove a newer session's cookie.
judgement.why: State 6 fixes the complete attribute set, omits every lifetime attribute by allowing no others, and State 5 specifies replacement rather than expiry or deletion.

topics.topic: Meaning and enforcement of the owner-session cookie's own-origin scope
questions: Does “own origin” mean the owner interface's scheme-host-port origin, or only the host/path scope that browser cookie attributes can enforce; if it means the former, what prevents the cookie being sent to the service API on another port of the same host?

quotes:
The session cookie is
  named `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` (`__Host-registry_session`) and set
  with the attributes `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES` holds and no other:
  `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `Path=/` and no `Domain`, which the `__Host-` prefix
  makes a browser require (A13 rule 1), and `SameSite=Strict`, so a browser
  never sends it with a request another site started (owner, 2026-11-24;
  OWASP).
judgement.why: State 6 chooses the browser-enforceable host-wide `__Host-` cookie scope with `Path=/` and no `Domain`; it specifies no port isolation, so the generator does not have to choose among alternative origin-enforcement mechanisms.

topics.topic: Whether and how sign-out must expire the browser session cookie
questions: When sign-out ends the server-side session, must the owner interface also expire the browser cookie, and if so must the deletion repeat the same Path, Domain and other scoping attributes?

quotes:
Registry never expires or deletes the cookie: an ended session's
cookie is refused at the session check and replaced by the next sign-in, so
no answer, however late it arrives, can remove a newer session's cookie.
judgement.why: State 5 explicitly requires sign-out to leave the browser cookie in place and rely on refusal of its ended session identity.
